$comment: One price schedule — GitHub issue #366, DECISIONS.md § D525 clause 2, docs/38 § 2.1. Every price a player pays for a change, in one place, so the same change costs the same in Scenario, in Career and in the fix-a-building editor. The figures are DRAFTED, not measured: a price is game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's. Where two shipped lists already agreed the agreed figure is kept and said so; where they disagreed the disagreement is recorded in the entry's note. See packages/viz/src/pricing/parse.ts.

tiers.name: Dispatcher
tiers.note: How the cars are told to behave. Nothing is installed and nothing is cut, so it is the cheap end of the ladder and tuning is nearly free.

tiers.name: Equipment
tiers.note: Settings and fittings on kit the building already has — door timings, sensors, landing panels. Dearer than telling the cars what to do, cheaper than changing the building.

tiers.name: Building
tiers.note: The fabric: a new shaft or car, a faster or larger machine, a rezoned bank. The dearest end, and the only one that books long works.

changes.name: Where idle cars wait
changes.note: Free in every shipped list. Four fix cases price the idle strategy at 0 units and none prices it higher.

changes.name: How calls are assigned
changes.note: The fix cases price an assignment-mode change at 2 units as a diagnosis and at 8 as a costly fix. 2 is taken: the 8 was a case where the same press also bought a split threshold, which is priced on its own row now.

changes.name: How long doors are told to hold
changes.note: Telling the controller when to close, as opposed to re-fitting the door. Priced at 2 and 4 in the two cases that buy it; 3 is the midpoint.

changes.name: Trim the door dwell
changes.note: Set on doors already hung. Seventeen fix repairs buy it at 1, 2 or 3 units for the SAME settings — the clearest case in the tree of one change carrying three prices. 2 is the mode.

changes.name: Faster doors
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Better sensors
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Advance opening
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Zone the tower
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept. Grouping calls is a landing-side fitting rather than a cut shaft.

changes.name: Destination panels
changes.note: Two lists agree on 13: the campaign shop's Control tier 2, and the dearest of the four fix repairs that install them. § D112's line is kept — TUNING a destination dispatcher is dispatcher-tier and nearly free; INSTALLING the panels is this row. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: issue #366's table lists panels under building while its prose puts them under equipment. Equipment is taken, because the prose cites § D112 and the table does not.

changes.name: Full destination dispatch
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Move or stagger a tenancy
changes.note: Three fix cases price a floor-population change at 2 or 3 units as a diagnosis; the shop prices moving a tenant floor at 20 with four nights. 2 is taken for the fix-case row and the shop's own row is kept separately below, because they are not the same act: staggering start times is a letter, and moving a tenant is a lease.

changes.name: Queue marshalling
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Staggered start times
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Move a tenant floor
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Rezone a bank
changes.note: Twelve fix repairs buy it between 0 and 12 units with no rule relating the price to how much is rezoned. 6 is the midpoint and the widest draft in this file.

changes.name: A faster machine
changes.note: THE CLEAREST CONFLICT THE SCHEDULE RESOLVES. The same purchase — make a machine faster — was priced three ways: the fix cases charge 8, 9 or 10 units for a 0.5 m/s bump and 12 for 1.0; `fixit/engine.ts#EDITOR_PRICING.speedUnitsPerHalfMps` charges 6; the campaign shop's machine tiers are 14, 25 and 40. A player paid a different price for the same metre per second depending on which screen they stood on. 10 is taken — the fix cases' mode — so the editor's step moves 6 to 10.

changes.name: Larger cars
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure for 16-person cars, kept. The editor's per-two-places step is a separate row (`larger-car-step`), because re-specifying the fleet and widening one car are different acts.

changes.name: A new car in a new shaft
changes.note: FOUR shipped lists independently say 34: every one of the eighteen fix cases' new-shaft repair, `fixit/parse.ts#NEW_SHAFT_UNITS`, `fixit/engine.ts#EDITOR_PRICING.shaftUnits`, and the campaign shop's Shafts tier 1. Nothing here is drafted — this figure was already unanimous and is only being moved.

changes.name: A fifth car
changes.note: The campaign shop's own figure, kept.

changes.name: Two more places in a car
changes.note: Kept from `fixit/engine.ts#EDITOR_PRICING.capacityUnitsPerTwoPlaces`. Deliberately a separate row from `larger-cars`: adding two places to a car in the editor and re-specifying the fleet to 16-person cars are different acts, so they are two changes at two prices rather than one change at two prices, which is what #366 forbids.
